prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1458; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: At approximately the scene of a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, I found Driver 1 and Driver 2 operating vehicles that had come together nose to nose. Driver 1 is the named driver on the policy for the vehicle involved. Driver 2 reported neck and back strain and was evaluated at the scene. The reported symptoms are consistent with the type of impact described by both drivers. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general position of the vehicles and some areas of contact, but they do not show whether all of the visible damage resulted from this collision. No independent witnesses were located. Driver 1 and Passenger both stated that Driver 2 was in the vehicle at the time of impact, and this was not disputed. Neither vehicle had any prior damage known to the parties or noted during the inspection. Further review of the damage is recommended to determine the extent to which it can be attributed to this incident.
